questions.q: Why should you be cautious about publicly sharing screenshots from an Oracle Fusion Cloud environment?
options: Screenshots are always completely safe to publish without any consideration
Oracle Fusion Cloud is licensed software, and terms of use governing what can be shared may apply even to screens you personally configured
Oracle Fusion has no visual interface to screenshot at all
Screenshots are only a concern for Payables, not other modules
questions.explain: Because Oracle Fusion Cloud is licensed, login-gated enterprise software, terms of use may restrict sharing screenshots - even of screens you configured yourself - so caution and checking the specific terms is the safer default.

questions.q: Which portfolio artifact is described as being entirely your own original writing, and therefore safe to share?
options: A screenshot of a live Oracle Fusion instance
A copy of Oracle's own internal documentation
A requirements and configuration workbook written in your own words
A recording of someone else's licensed training session
questions.explain: A requirements/configuration workbook, an issue log, original SQL, and a case study write-up are all your own original writing - unlike a screenshot of licensed software.

questions.q: What does an issue log, written in the style of the capstone's close, actually demonstrate to a reader?
options: That you can diagnose and fix real problems, not just perform configuration steps
That you have memorized every Oracle menu item
That you can operate a spreadsheet
That you have access to a licensed Oracle environment
questions.explain: An issue log documenting symptom, root cause, fix, and verification demonstrates the diagnostic skill covered in lesson 9 - distinct from simply listing configuration tasks performed.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what question should every portfolio piece answer in one sentence before the reader gets into the detail?
options: "How many hours did this take to build?"
"What software license was used to build this?"
"Who else has seen this document?"
"What does this prove I can do?"
questions.explain: Leading with a single clear sentence answering 'what does this prove I can do?' orients the reader before they dig into supporting detail.

questions.q: Why is original SQL written during the SQL-for-Oracle-Financials coursework a safe thing to share in a portfolio?
options: Because it is your own original writing, not a screenshot of licensed software
Because SQL queries are never covered by any licensing terms anywhere
Because it must first be approved by Oracle Corporation directly
Because it automatically counts as official Oracle certification
questions.explain: Original SQL you personally wrote is your own intellectual output, unlike a screenshot of a licensed vendor's software interface - making it safe to include in a public portfolio.
